title: Northern California & Southern Oregon
dek: A ~1,100-mile loop from the Golden Gate up the redwood coast, across southern Oregon, down past Mount Shasta and Lassen, and home through Napa and Sonoma wine country.

days.label: Day 1
prose: Scenic ride via US-101 and CA-1 north, mixing coastal beauty, redwoods and small towns.
sights: bridge and coast views; winding roads
cliffs and waves; optional lighthouse detour (~20 mi)
harbor, seafood, “The Birds” film site; exhilarating CA-1 curves
orchards and farm stands via CA-12 E
tasting and gardens (~7 mi from Santa Rosa)
days.tips: Early morning or late afternoon for golden light and less fog. CA-1 is tight and thrilling but watch for fog and wind; US-101 is faster and straighter. Plan one or two stops (Stinson Beach, Bodega Bay, Kendall-Jackson) on the ~3 hr 53 min ride. Fuel at Bodega — stations are sparse on CA-1.
dangers: Coastal fog on CA-1
Dense morning fog near Stinson Beach and Point Reyes reduces visibility; use low beams and fog lights and slow down. Avoid a pre-9 AM start if foggy (check Caltrans QuickMap).
Tight curves, wet pavement
CA-1’s sharp turns (e.g. near Bodega) get slick from fog and drizzle; stay focused and avoid gravel shoulders. US-101 is straighter but watch the vineyard winds.
Construction
Northbound US-101 reduced to one lane ~2–3 mi north of SR-271 (Mendocino Co.) around the clock — expect delays. One-way traffic control near Arnold possible 7 AM–5 PM.
Wildlife
Deer are active in Marin and Sonoma at dawn and dusk (e.g. Hendy Woods); slow down in forested areas.
Fuel
Sparse stations on CA-1; fill up in SF or Sausalito.

lodging.name: Hampton Inn Ukiah
lodging.desc: Clean, modern, motorcycle-friendly parking. Free breakfast, Wi-Fi, pool. Near US-101 and downtown.

dining: Japanese and sushi; cozy, fresh rolls like the Mendocino, and tempura. Open until ~9 PM.

days.label: Day 2
prose: The Redwood Highway (US-101 north) through forests, coast and towns.
sights: 31 mi through Humboldt Redwoods SP; Founders Grove, Rockefeller Loop
Victorian town; Old Town marina detour
wetlands, ocean vistas; elk at Elk Prairie
Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park
days.tips: 4–5 hours without stops; plan 6–8 with sights. Tight curves in the redwoods and along the coast; fog and wet roads are common in the morning. Fuel in Ukiah, Willits or Eureka (scarce in the redwoods). Watch for elk and deer.
dangers: Fog and rain in the redwoods
Morning fog and drizzle on US-101 near Eureka and Del Norte; use fog lights and consider delaying the start to 10 AM. Fallen leaves and needles make curves slick.
Fuel
Limited between Garberville and Eureka — fill early. Check for debris in the redwoods.

lodging.name: Lighthouse Inn
lodging.desc: Cozy coastal vibe, ocean views, free breakfast and Wi-Fi. Spacious lot for bikes.

dining: Seafood with harbor views — crab and clams. Open until ~8 PM.

days.label: Day 3
prose: US-199 (the Redwood Highway) to Grants Pass, OR-238 through the Applegate Valley to Medford, then OR-140 to Klamath Falls.
sights: Stout Grove detour on Howland Hill Rd
turquoise water and cliffs; Patrick Creek Overlook
vineyards and orchards; Applegate Lake stop
optional OR-46 detour (~20 mi) to marble caves
Fish Lake / Lake of the Woods
optional, ~70 mi round trip; Rim Drive vistas
days.tips: 3.5–4 hours base; 5–7 with detours. Curvy and twisty on US-199 and OR-46; low traffic on OR-238. Fuel in Grants Pass or Medford. Bring layers for the coastal chill and inland warmth.
dangers: Fog and wet roads
Morning fog on US-199 (Jedediah Smith); careful on curves and in the tunnel. OR-46 (Caves detour) is narrow and slick when wet — skip it if raining.
Twisty sections, wildlife

Tight turns on US-199 and OR-46 — watch for gravel and debris. Deer and elk around Applegate and Lake of the Woods at dawn and dusk. OR-140 width-restricted to 14 ft near Klamath Falls for construction.

lodging.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Klamath Falls
lodging.desc: Modern, central, secure parking. Free breakfast, pool, Wi-Fi. Near OR-140 and downtown.

dining: Thai — pad Thai and curry. Open until ~9 PM.

days.label: Day 4
prose: US-97 south to Mount Shasta, CA-89 south and CA-44 through Lassen Volcanic National Park to Redding, then I-5 south to Red Bluff.
sights: vista point near Weed; optional CA-89 detour via McCloud for river and falls
lava fields and Lassen Peak views
Manzanita Lake, Sulphur Works, Bumpass Hell, Kings Creek / Summit Lake
days.tips: 6–8 hours with stops. Thrilling CA-89 switchbacks; bring layers for the elevation swings. Fuel in Klamath Falls, Weed, Burney or Redding.
dangers: Elevation weather
Sudden changes in Lassen (CA-89); light rain or snow possible at the peaks — check NPS road status (usually open in October, but early snow can close it).
Wildlife and curves
Deer and bears around Lassen and Burney; slow down in forests. CA-89 and CA-44 descents are tight; watch gravel shoulders at dawn and dusk.
Heat
85°F+ in Red Bluff — hydrate. I-5 is straightforward but crosswinds are possible.

lodging.name: Hampton Inn & Suites Red Bluff
lodging.desc: Highly rated, clean and modern. Breakfast, Wi-Fi, pool. Near I-5 and the river.

dining: BBQ — tri-tip and ribs. Open until ~8 PM.

days.label: Day 5
prose: I-5 south to Williams, CA-20 west to Clearlake, CA-53 and CA-29 south to Calistoga, then CA-12 west to Sonoma.
sights: almond and rice fields, Sierra views
rolling hills and oaks; Mount Konocti volcano
lake views and Lower Lake towns
vineyards, Mayacamas Mountains, balloons, Calistoga springs
oak hills and horse ranches to Sonoma Plaza
days.tips: Balances straight I-5 cruising with CA-20 and CA-12 curves. Go early for fewer tourists. Watch for winery traffic and cyclists on CA-29 and CA-12.
dangers: Crosswinds and traffic
Open I-5 stretches are gusty (15–20 mph) — lean in. Heavy tourist traffic on CA-29 and CA-12 (winery pullouts, cyclists), especially afternoons.
Curves and roadwork
Moderate twists on CA-20 and CA-12 near Clear Lake and Sonoma; gravel possible if damp. Utility work on CA-20 at Clearlake Oaks and night paving on CA-29 west of Lower Lake.
Wildlife
Deer on CA-20 and CA-12 at dawn and dusk.
